header: For five years, AKA was a research studio working on decentralized identity. Then the AI era gave the company a new direction, and it needed a teaser site to reflect it. I designed and built the site from scratch.

layout.title: Background
text: In the history of a startup, the time you launch is a pivotal moment. Before you launch, no one knows what you do, so people's curiosity is an asset. I created the teaser site to lean into that curiosity.

At the time, Twitter was full of people using Open Claw, and they were seeing their databases getting deleted by AI agents. It was a real problem, and everyone building with agents had felt it. And aka was working on a solution to the problem.
So the site became a visualization of this idea of AI agents running wild.

layout.title: Under the hood
text: I built the site in React and Three.js, rendering with WebGPU and custom shaders for the cords' materials. Older browsers don't support WebGPU, but since most of the audience was technical, we built for it first and added a WebGL2 fallback so everyone else still sees a version of it. For the physics of the cords, the bounce, weight, etc., I used Rapier, a JavaScript physics engine.
Everything was composed in full 3D, then locked in place in a 2D view.

media.title: A few of the dozen-plus experiments along the way

text: To make precise adjustments along the way, I built an editing layer on top. This let me adjust the cords in real time, tune the physics, and move the camera.

layout.title: Result
text: The relaunch went great. Within a couple of weeks, hundreds of people had joined aka's waitlist.

Before AI, a site like this meant an agency team, or weeks of feedback rounds with a developer. Now I could design directly in code. And the overlay I built let me adjust the cords, physics, and camera right in the browser and see every change instantly.
